title: Mathematical Structure of Charged-Particle Dynamics in Curved Spacetime
content:
How does the geometry of spacetime enter the equation of motion of a charged particle? We study a test charge obeying the covariant Lorentz force law \(u^

Geometry acts through the connection, through the metric that defines measured energies and fields, and through isometries. We prove that every Killing vector preserving \(F\) yields a gauge-invariant constant of motion and that Killing observers measure \(d(N\gamma)/d	au = eNE_\mu u^\mu\), so the magnetic field they see never does work. In the Reissner–Nordström spacetime a charge can hover only if \(eQ > M\), at a radius given in closed form, and every sub-extremal equilibrium is unstable with Killing-time rate \(\kappa_+ (r_+/r_{\mathrm{eq}})^2\). The ISCO condition is a polynomial in \(e^2\); for \(|e| = 1\) it gives \(r_{\mathrm{ISCO}} = 3M + \sqrt{9M^2 - 6Q^2}\) for both signs of the charge. For a Schwarzschild black hole in Wald's uniform magnetic field we solve for the angular velocity of circular orbits and prove that only anti-Larmor orbits exist inside the photon sphere. All results are verified symbolically and numerically.
